findings.source_text: no man is ignorant, Eccl. Pol. Lib. 1.
findings.candidate_text: …who are as ourselves.” (Hooker, Ecclesiastical Polity, book I)
findings.problem: Citation is wrapped in parentheses, while the style note's form and the later chapters (ch6, ch7, ch8, ch11) use the bare form 'Hooker, Ecclesiastical Polity, book I, section N' after the quotation. There is no section number because the source gives none, which is correct.
findings.suggested_fix: …who are as ourselves.” Hooker, Ecclesiastical Polity, book I.

findings.source_text: the judicious Hooker, Eccl. Pol. lib. i. sect. 10, where he says,
findings.candidate_text: the authority of the judicious Hooker, where he says (Hooker, Ecclesiastical Polity, book I, section 10):
findings.problem: The citation repeats 'Hooker' straight after the name and moves it after 'where he says', so it reads awkwardly. Content and section number are correct.
findings.suggested_fix: the authority of the judicious Hooker (Ecclesiastical Polity, book I, section 10), where he says:

findings.source_text: permits me my own defence, and the right of war, a liberty to kill the aggressor, because the aggressor allows not time to appeal
findings.candidate_text: for a life, once lost, can never be repaired. For the aggressor leaves no time to appeal to our common judge
findings.problem: Two reason clauses in a row ('for a life…', 'For the aggressor…') make the second reason seem to hang loose. In Locke it explains why the law grants the liberty to kill the aggressor. The meaning is intact, including the thief/robber point that one may kill only when the law cannot step in against present force, but the logic is blurred.
findings.suggested_fix: …for a life, once lost, can never be repaired. The law allows this because the aggressor leaves no time to appeal to our common judge, or for the law to decide, in a case where the harm may be irreparable.

findings.source_text: which (the inhabitants thereof not having joined with the rest of mankind, in the consent of the use of their common money) lie waste
findings.candidate_text: which lie waste, because their inhabitants have not joined the rest of mankind in consenting to the use of their common money
findings.problem: Locke puts the fact in a parenthetical circumstance. The candidate turns it into an explicit cause of the land lying waste, which slightly strengthens the claim. The causal reading is defensible, but it is interpretive.
findings.suggested_fix: which lie waste (their inhabitants not having joined the rest of mankind in consenting to the use of their common money)

findings.source_text: feeds, lodges, and is clad worse than a day-labourer in England
findings.candidate_text: eats, lives and dresses worse than a day labourer in England
findings.problem: 'lives' is vaguer than 'lodges' (housing). The prior version's close wording was clear, so this change was gratuitous and lost a little precision.
findings.suggested_fix: is fed, housed and clothed worse than a day labourer in England

findings.source_text: than several nations of the Americans are of this
findings.candidate_text: than several nations of the Americans give of this
findings.problem: 'several' keeps Locke's sense of 'various/many', but a modern reader takes it as 'a few'. Also, 'give of this' is stiff.
findings.suggested_fix: There could be no clearer proof of this than the many nations of the Americas.

findings.problem: The prior 'where the strongest carries the day' was clear and accurate. The rewording, like much of this paragraph ('source' for 'fountain', 'protest against so loudly'), is gratuitous but harmless.

findings.source_text: this was only to drudgery, not to slavery
findings.candidate_text: this was only into hard service, not into slavery
findings.problem: 'drudgery' (kept in the prior) is current English and Locke's own word. 'hard service' is an unnecessary change, though meaning is preserved. The Exod. xxi. completion is correct.
findings.suggested_fix: But plainly this was only into drudgery, not into slavery.

findings.source_text: what portion a man carved to himself, was easily seen
findings.candidate_text: The portion a man cut out for himself was easy to see
findings.problem: The prior 'carved to himself' / 'carve himself too much' was clear, and the change is cosmetic. The completion 'take more than he needed' matches raw.txt line 1158.
'owner' is accurate, but 'proprietor' keeps the visible link to 'property' that the argument depends on (the prior kept it). Consider restoring.
findings.suggested_fix: master of himself and proprietor of his own person and of its actions or labour

findings.source_text: to distinguish these powers one from wealth, a father of a family, and a captain of a galley
findings.candidate_text: to tell these powers apart from one another, and to show the difference between a ruler of a commonwealth, a father of a family, and a captain of a galley
findings.problem: The Gutenberg §2 corruption is correctly repaired with the standard reading (raw.txt also has the corrupt text), as the style note documents. The extra 'commonwealth' in this paragraph comes from that repair.

summary: No major fidelity defects in the sampled or specifically checked paragraphs of chapters 1–5. The five truncated chapter endings are completed correctly against raw.txt ('public good.', 'very clear.', 'supreme judge of all men.', 'Exod. xxi.', 'more than he needed.'). The §2 corruption repair, the removal of the leaked 'Sect, 10.' in ch2 p8 (content intact), the ch3 p3 thief/robber reasoning, and ch5 p21 'seed' are all correct. In ch5, the labour-mixing argument, the spoilage limit ('as much as anyone can make use of … before it spoils'), the 'enough, and as good, left in common for others' proviso (p2, p8), money by tacit consent (p25, p28) and property/possession usage all match the source term for term. A term-count comparison found no 'property' flattened into 'possessions', and no 'legislature', 'state of warfare' or 'natural condition'. Remaining issues are a minor Hooker citation-form inconsistency (ch2 p3, p13), a couple of small interpretive or precision slips, and a few gratuitous rewordings of already-clear prior sentences. Most other changes from the prior version were justified, removing leftover archaisms such as 'prejudice', 'presently', 'straitened', and the Hooker passages that had been left unmodernized.
